newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels kidnap helicopter crew.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels kidnap helicopter crew.

text.p: Leftist rebels claimed responsibility on Sunday for the kidnapping of all three crew members of a civilian helicopter that disappeared while on a flight over Colombia's northwest Choco province.
The Russian-made Mi-17 helicopter was found intact on Sunday, a day after it disappeared, in a jungle-covered area outside Choco's provincial capital Quibdo, police and military officials said.

But they said there was no sign of the crew members and a caller, identifying himself as a member of the National Liberation Army (ELN), later told the Caracol radio station all three were safely in the hands of ELN rebels who were holding them in exchange for a ransom payment.
"They (the ELN) have claimed responsibility for the kidnapping and they say they'll blow up the helicopter if anyone tries to recover it," a reporter at Caracol told Reuters.

The ELN, a Cuban-inspired group founded by radical Roman Catholic priests in 1966, specialises in kidnappings and attacks on oil and coal projects across the country. It claimed responsibility earlier this month for shooting down another Mi- 17 over northeastern Arauca province -- an attack in which 20 soldiers and one civilian crew member were killed.
The missing helicopter crew members in Choco, including a Nicaraguan-born flight engineer, had been contracted to install posts for electrical pylons, authorities said.
